roadmap.goal: A bound Delivery's name, date and membership follow Jira on their own, on the Portfolio refresh that already runs. A date that has moved into the past is accepted and says so on screen; a read that failed leaves the last known values and does not take the refresh down; a Delivery somebody retired is never written to.

phases.title: The one write a hand is refused

steps.goal: Delivery.SyncFromSource writes the three things the source owns, refuses a Delivery that follows nothing and one that has been retired, and moves the version an open browser holds only when something actually moved.
criteria: A past date from the source is accepted; the hand-entry guard one layer up still refuses one.
A refresh that found nothing new leaves the concurrency token where it was.
The last-heard-from stamp is the DAY, so re-reading an unchanged source on the same day writes the same value back and the row stays out of the save.

steps.goal: DeliverySourceSyncService groups the bound Deliveries by the kind of source they follow and asks once per kind, so a Portfolio with fifty costs the refresh what one does.
criteria: Only a source that resolved to a live object writes anything; NotFound, NoDate and Unavailable all leave the Delivery as it stands - slice 03 owns telling them apart on screen.
The connection is asked whether it still offers the source before it is asked about one, so a withdrawal arrives as itself rather than as a throw indistinguishable from a blip.
A source that throws, and an answer the aggregate refuses, each cost their own Deliveries a refresh and no others.

phases.title: On the refresh that already happens

steps.goal: PortfolioUpdater runs the pass beside the rule re-match. No new background service, no new schedule, no new setting.
criteria: It runs after the Feature fetch it narrows against, before the one save that keeps what it says, and before the forecast that raises the event the daily snapshot records the target from.

steps.goal: The owed wiring scenario: re-sync driven through the scheduled refresh rather than through the service, read back the way the grid reads it.
criteria: A Release renamed and rescheduled in Jira reaches the Delivery with nobody asking.
A refresh that found nothing new records that it asked, so the scenario cannot pass with the sync deleted.
A retired Delivery is left where it was however far its Release moved.

phases.title: Say when the target has been and gone

steps.goal: A Delivery whose target day has passed says Overdue.
criteria: Decided on the instance's day by the backend, not on the reader's browser clock.
The day of the target itself is not overdue.
It is a fact about the date, so a hand-maintained Delivery says it too.
